title: The Phantom Warning
text: I was drifting through town, lost in thought, when I stepped into the street without looking. A piercing shriek sliced through the air—an old woman, her voice cracking like dead leaves, screamed for me to stop. I froze and turned just in time to see a bus thunder past, a blast of air clawing at my face. My heart pounded as I looked across to thank her, but the street was empty. No trace of her remained. That’s when the chill set in—she looked exactly like my grandmother, who we buried seven years ago. I still remember the floral scarf she wore... the same one we buried her in.

title: The Pianist's Lament
text: We wandered into the skeleton of an abandoned theater, its air thick with forgotten breath. As we crept through its crumbling halls, a piano melody began to drift—low, haunting, almost mournful. It drew us to the stage, where a dust-veiled piano sat, keys untouched, strings long dead. Then he appeared: a tall, gaunt figure in tattered evening wear, standing in the balcony like a relic of grief. He stared down at us, his eyes hollow with memory, before dissolving into nothingness. Later, I learned of the fire—the pianist who perished mid-performance, still searching for his final ovation.

title: The Clockmaker's Secret
text: The alley behind the old square was silent except for the ticking. Hundreds of clocks lined the walls of a forgotten shop, all moving in perfect rhythm though none were wound. I stepped inside and found an old man bent over a workbench, his fingers motionless above shattered gears. He looked up slowly and whispered my name, though we had never met. Then every clock stopped at once. The room darkened, and when I blinked, the shop was gone. Later, locals told me the clockmaker died decades ago the night his son vanished—and ever since, strangers hear the ticking when someone is about to disappear.

title: A Ghostly Encounter
text: I was trying to sleep when I heard slow footsteps outside my bedroom door. At first, I thought it was just the old wooden floor creaking because of the cold weather. But then the footsteps stopped right in front of my room. A few seconds later, I heard three soft knocks on the door. My heart started racing. I checked my phone — 2:13 AM. Everyone else in the house was asleep. Gathering some courage, I opened the door slowly… but the hallway was completely empty. As I turned back toward my bed, I froze. There was a dark figure standing near the window, staring directly at me with pale white eyes. Before I could scream, the room suddenly became freezing cold and the figure disappeared into the darkness. The next morning, I found muddy footprints near the window… even though it had not rained for days.
I saw a shadow near the trees...  Suddenly my screen started flickering.

title: An invisible man sighting in pune.
